notes: §1985:VIII.4.7.3 SR3: "The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is specified for file-name-1". The 1985 text defines neither "applicable" nor "appropriate", and two final adjudications read it opposite ways (2026-11-12, kb/Work PB5413 amendment 1: reading A, a mode procedure is applicable to a statement of any file that can be open in that mode; 2026-11-14, op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json q1: reading B, only a mode in which the statement's condition can arise). So it is implementor latitude, and WiseOwl COBOL takes reading A as a DOCUMENTED LATITUDE CHOICE (kb/Work PB5591; docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.5; docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D31(a)): reading B would refuse CCVS-85 SQ148A, GnuCOBOL 3.2 -std=cobol85 enforces none of the mandatory-phrase rules and so does not decide, and rejecting legal source is the worse harm. ExceptionPhraseRequirement.HasApplicableUse implements it: a declarative naming the file, or one for an open mode the file can be open in (EXTEND only for a file that can be opened EXTEND, kb/Work PB5413), refuses COBOL6826 otherwise. The witness (pb5591_relative_output_use_excuses_phrases_85) runs at --std 85: the statement with no phrase is accepted under the one mode declarative, and at run time the procedure takes the logic-error status the statement raises in that mode (47, 48 or 49), matching the expectation derived from the text. The adjudication's probe (refute-rs-10/st/st_seq_useextend.cob (ON EXTEND only; the defect) and st_io.cob (ON I-O only; correctly accepted)) observed: both compile with no diagnostic and print AFTER START 23; exit 0, no procedure ran; under reading A that is the conforming result. Previous verdict: PARTIAL, held on reading B. Recorded 2026-11-14 by records-85-held from the final held-row adjudication (op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json).

next.reason: §1985:VIII.4.7.3 SR3 (level 2, boxed; the box is no difference): 'The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is specified for file-name-1' (START on a relative file). 2023 has no such syntax rule (§2023:14.9.41.3); §2023:14.9.41.4 GR6 makes the transfer of control depend 'on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases in the START statement as specified in 9.1.14', and the refused case is stated by §2023:9.1.14 GR4: 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'; so too §2023:9.1.14 GR3: 'If control is returned from those statements or there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'. Words that differ: 1985 'must be specified'; 2023 'not specified ... there are no applicable ... exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end'. A statement 1985 refuses is accepted by 2023 with a stated run-time effect: a lifted refusal, so CHANGED (kb/Work PB5021), not REMOVED.
